objects.definition: typedef struct PACKET_OID_DATA { uint32_t Oid; uint32_t Length; uint8_t Data[1]; } PACKET_OID_DATA, *PPACKET_OID_DATA;
objects.description: Opaque-style structure used to carry an OID request/response. Fields: Oid is the OID code, Length is the size in bytes of the valid payload in Data, and Data is a 1-byte flexible array placeholder for variable-length data. The macro PACKET_OID_DATA_LENGTH(n) computes the total size needed for an instance with n bytes of Data. Allocation must account for the variable payload; do not access beyond the allocated Data length.

objects.definition: struct bpf_insn { uint16_t code; uint8_t jt; uint8_t jf; uint32_t k; };
objects.description: Single Berkeley Packet Filter (BPF) instruction. Fields encode the opcode (code), jump offsets for true/false branches (jt/jf), and an immediate/constant or other operand (k). Used within a bpf_program to define a filter.

objects.definition: struct bpf_program { uint32_t bf_len; struct bpf_insn* bf_insns; };
objects.description: A compiled BPF filter program consisting of bf_len instructions stored at bf_insns. The program is typically applied to packets by kernel/userland BPF engines. Memory management of bf_insns is external to this header and not specified here.

objects.definition: struct bpf_stat { uint32_t bs_recv; uint32_t bs_drop; uint32_t ps_ifdrop; uint32_t bs_capt; };
objects.description: Statistics structure for BPF capture: total packets received (bs_recv), dropped by filter/buffer (bs_drop), dropped by interface (ps_ifdrop), and captured/accepted (bs_capt). Exact semantics may vary by implementation.

objects.definition: struct bpf_hdr { struct timeval bh_tstamp; uint32_t bh_caplen; uint32_t bh_datalen; uint16_t bh_hdrlen; };
objects.description: Per-packet BPF header preceding captured packet data. Includes timestamp (bh_tstamp), captured length (bh_caplen), original wire length (bh_datalen), and header length (bh_hdrlen) to locate payload. Commonly used when reading from BPF devices or files.
No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only contains preprocessor macros for driver/service names. Therefore there are no custom data types to document.

Alias for a pointer to constant, null-terminated C string. Commonly used to represent read-only strings returned by the API such as version or driver names. Note that it points to const char; do not modify the underlying characters.

functions.name: PacketGetVersion
functions.description: Returns a read-only C string with the version of the Packet library or component. Intended for displaying or logging the library version. Call with no arguments and use the returned pointer as a null-terminated string.
requirements: The returned LPCSTR is read-only; the caller must not modify the string contents.
Ownership/lifetime of the returned pointer is unspecified in this header; the caller must not attempt to free it.
Interpret the return value as a null-terminated C string.

functions.name: PacketGetDriverVersion
functions.description: Returns a read-only C string with the version of the underlying Packet driver. Useful for diagnostics and compatibility checks. Call with no arguments and use the returned pointer as a null-terminated string.
requirements: The returned LPCSTR is read-only; the caller must not modify the string contents.
Ownership/lifetime of the returned pointer is unspecified in this header; the caller must not attempt to free it.
Interpret the return value as a null-terminated C string.

functions.name: PacketGetDriverName
functions.description: Returns a read-only C string with the name of the underlying Packet driver. Useful for identifying which driver is in use. Call with no arguments and use the returned pointer as a null-terminated string.
requirements: The returned LPCSTR is read-only; the caller must not modify the string contents.
Ownership/lifetime of the returned pointer is unspecified in this header; the caller must not attempt to free it.
Interpret the return value as a null-terminated C string.
